preamble: The voiced alveolar lateral fricative [ɮ] loses its frication and becomes the lateral approximant [l]. The documented case is Yami (Tao) of Orchid Island, Taiwan, where /l/ is traditionally realized as [ɮ] before /i/ (soli [ʂuɮi] 'taro'); younger, Mandarin-dominant speakers increasingly replace this [ɮ] with plain [l]. Lai and Hsu (2013) link the rate of change to Mandarin competence, Mandarin-speaking frequency and weaker ties to the Yami community, since Mandarin has no lateral fricative.

examples.note: Contact-induced change in progress: speakers with stronger Mandarin competence and weaker Yami social networks show the highest rate of [ɮ] > [l].

sources: Lai, L.-F., & Hsu, H. (2013). Contact-induced sound change: analysis of the alveolar lateral fricative in Yami. Journal of Estonian and Finno-Ugric Linguistics, 4(2), 31-50. https://doi.org/10.12697/jeful.2013.4.2.02
